authority: User confirmed multiplayer, quests and party creation on 2026-10-23
confirmed_scope: DuTraveller is a multiplayer game. Player gameplay data must be correctly replicated with appropriate ownership and visibility.
Quest gameplay includes guild, personal, party, class and area quests. Follow QuestGameplayContract.json for ownership, eligibility, shared progress and reward requirements.
Party creation and membership are part of the restoration scope.
Player currency and guild settlement/economy state are also authoritative multiplayer systems. Follow GuildEconomyWorldContract.json for building, crafting, vendors, farming and main-world evidence.
implementation_requirements: The server owns authoritative gameplay state and validates requests to spend points, learn/equip skills, activate abilities, acquire/move/use/drop items, equip items and receive rewards.
Replicate each state field to its intended audience. Private inventories, unspent points and detailed progression are not automatically public to every client.
Clients cannot select another player's state as the mutation target. Derive request ownership from the authenticated owning connection and validate referenced actors/items.
Replicated attributes, equipment effects, learned skill ranks, hotbar assignments, inventory, quest state and party membership must initialize and update the correct local UI.
Equipment bonuses, ability effects, item transfers and rewards apply once on the server; client notifications and replication do not apply them again.
Restore quest acceptance, objective progression, completion, turn-in and rewards using server-validated gameplay events.
Restore party creation and membership with server-validated state transitions. Recover supported invite, join, leave, leader and disconnect behavior from original evidence.
Recover persistence and reconnect/travel behavior for player progression, inventory, quests and parties rather than assuming all state shares one lifetime.
rules_requiring_original_evidence: Listen-server, dedicated-server, peer hosting and session discovery requirements
Party size, invite/accept rules, leadership transfer, kick permissions and persistence
Individual versus shared quest progress, party eligibility and shared reward rules
Loot ownership, trading, reward distribution and item visibility
Which stats, equipment details, quest markers and party information other players may see
acceptance_checks: Test with at least two distinct connected players, including a remote client, and ensure state remains associated with the correct player.
Spend attribute/skill points and equip items from the remote client; verify authoritative balances, bonuses, resulting effects and local UI converge without duplication.
Verify visible equipment and combat presentation on another client while private data stays restricted to its intended audience.
Validate server-side ability eligibility, resources, cooldowns, targets and damage independently of client UI.
Test concurrent item pickup and repeated requests for spending, crafting and quest rewards against authoritative balances and eligibility.
Exercise quest acceptance, objective updates, completion and rewards on separate players and with a party according to recovered sharing rules.
Exercise party creation and supported membership transitions, including a departing or disconnected member, without stale membership or another player's UI/state being overwritten.
Verify initialization, late joins and supported travel/reconnect flows; test the actual hosting mode once established.
implementation_status: Requirements captured. Replication, quest completion and party functionality have not been established as implemented or tested by the current inspection.
